record.original_question: Does every height-three complete intersection have the strong Lefschetz property? More generally, does the same hold for complete intersections of larger height, for example Artinian complete intersections of height four?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. Does every height three complete intersection has the SLP? Is this true for complete intersections of larger height, e.g., Artinian height four?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $R = K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. An Artinian graded $K$-algebra $A = R/I = \bigoplus_{i=0}^{D} A_i$ (with $A_D \neq 0$) is said to have the Strong Lefschetz Property (SLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that for every pair of integers $0 \le i \le i+k \le D$, the multiplication map
$$\times \ell^{k} : A_i \longrightarrow A_{i+k}$$
has maximal rank (i.e. is either injective or surjective). An Artinian complete intersection of height $n$ (or codimension $n$) is a quotient $A = R/(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ where $f_1,\dots,f_n$ is a homogeneous regular sequence in $R$, so that $A$ is a finite-dimensional graded $K$-algebra.

(a) Does every Artinian complete intersection of height $3$ over $K$ have the Strong Lefschetz Property?

(b) More generally, for every $n \ge 4$ (in particular for $n = 4$), does every Artinian complete intersection of height $n$ over $K$ have the Strong Lefschetz Property?
artifact.status_search_result: The Strong Lefschetz Property for arbitrary Artinian complete intersections in height three (and higher) over a field of characteristic zero is widely regarded as open. While SLP is known for monomial complete intersections (Stanley) and various special families, recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 arXiv papers on SLP of 0-dimensional complete intersections) explicitly state that the general height-three case remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On Strong Lefschetz Property of 0-dimensional complete intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Even in the specific case of 0-dimensional homogeneous complete intersections, the strong Lefschetz property is open in general.
status_evidence.claim: SLP for general 0-dimensional complete intersections is open.

status_evidence.title: A binary tree of complete intersections with the strong Lefschetz property
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs families of complete intersections having SLP, indicating the general problem is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to identify families of complete intersections with SLP.

status_evidence.title: Monomial Almost Complete Intersections and the Strong Lefschetz Property
status_evidence.snippet: Studies SLP for related classes; refers to general SLP question for complete intersections as conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-height SLP conjecture for complete intersections still under investigation.
